verdict.rationale: Working Copy lets you attach a private key to an Identity and keep SSH keys in the Secure Enclave behind Face ID or Touch ID, which is a first-party secure credential store. The docs also say the public key can be auto-registered with GitHub or BitBucket, implying one key serves several hosts. They never explicitly describe a central vault whose credentials are stored once and referenced per host, and they do not cover HTTPS passwords or tokens. missing for 10: explicit documentation of one credential reused across multiple hosts, vault coverage for HTTPS tokens/passwords, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can store credentials once in a secure vault and reference them from multiple hosts

citations.quote: For extra security SSH keys can reside on the Secure Enclave protected by Face ID or Touch ID.
You attach a private key to your Identity which can be imported or generated inside the app.
If you tap "Connect with BitBucket" or "Connect with GitHub" your public key will automatically be registered with BitBucket or GitHub.
